title: Quant path telemetry and latency-amortization strategy for mixed-precision kernels
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we expand INT8 and FP8 kernel coverage, the observed end-to-end latency variance for tail requests increased due to episodic dequantization and mixed-precision handoffs. Teams have limited visibility into how often requests traverse the full-precision vs quantized paths and whether the dequantization cost is being amortized across microbatches and KV-cache reuse.

Goal: Deliver instrumentation, lightweight telemetry, and a scheduling policy that: 1) surfaces per-request and per-model quant-path usage, 2) quantifies dequant overhead per-token and per-prefill/decode phase, and 3) implements a latency-amortization heuristic that coalesces dequant work across compatible microbatches or delays non-critical dequant until KV reuse is expected.

Scope:
- Add runtime counters and histograms for: path_taken (int8|fp8|fp16|fp32), dequant_time_ms, extra memcpy or allocation time, headwise quant conversions, and cache_hit_after_dequant.
- Export telemetry to our console/observability pipeline with tags: model, model_version, sequence_length_bucket, route (hosted|dedicated|private), and request_priority.
- Implement a scheduler prototype that groups short-prefill requests from the same model into a microbatch window (configurable) and performs a single dequant + shared KV-write to reduce aggregate dequant cost.
- Add a safe fallback so canary traffic uses conservative thresholds and production traffic sees the policy only after metric-based gating.

Non-goals: End-to-end kernel re-implementation; replacing existing kernel selection logic. This ticket focuses on telemetry and scheduling heuristics to reduce observed dequant-induced tail latency and provide the data to drive future kernel changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Telemetry emitted for >95% of renewals/sequence lengths and visible in Console per-route dashboard. 2) Bench harness shows >=10% p95 latency improvement for mixed-precision decode on the controlled canary with no correctness regressions. 3) Rollout gating metrics defined and an automated rollback if p99 latency increases >5% or token throughput reduction >3%.

2026-03-09 - QA notes (Jordan): Unit tests added for path tagging and coalescer timeouts. Integration test flakiness observed on small GPU instances due to host-side scheduling jitter; increased coalescer jitter tolerance and added deterministic test harness for CI. CI PR updated.
